lines.text: They saw it. Then forty six people died.
Point Pleasant, West Virginia. A small river town on the Ohio.
November fifteenth, 1966. Two young couples are driving near an old World War Two explosives plant the locals call the TNT area.
In their headlights, they say they saw a gray figure, taller than a man... with huge wings and glowing red eyes.
They floored it. They told the sheriff it kept up with their car... even at a hundred miles an hour.
The newspapers gave it a name. Mothman. And over the next year, dozens more people reported seeing it.
At rush hour, the Silver Bridge over the Ohio River collapsed. Thirty one vehicles fell into the water. Forty six people died.
Investigators traced it to one cracked steel link. But in town, people noticed something else. After the bridge fell... the sightings mostly stopped.
Skeptics say it was a large owl or a sandhill crane. Believers call it an omen. Today a steel Mothman statue stands downtown... and thousands come every September for the Mothman Festival.
So what did they see? Omen... or just an owl? Comment... and sleep tight, partner.
